exercise.name: Single-Arm High Cable Curl
library_steps: Stand side-on to a high pulley and hold the handle, arm out straight.
Keep your elbow at shoulder height and curl the handle to your head.
Straighten slowly, finish your reps, then switch arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing side-on to a high pulley, the working upper arm out to the sides at shoulder height; the elbows bend from ~12 to ~120 deg so the handles come toward the ears. Biceps does the work. The other hand rests on the hip.

setup.target: High pulleys (~1.75 m) on both sides.
Out to the side at shoulder height (~90 deg abduction), still.
Palms up, facing the head at the end.

movement.measure: upper arm from the torso side line

muscles.emg: Main elbow flexor in curls (EMG and hypertrophy, see sources).
muscles.role: Bends the elbow; what the exercise is for.

muscles.emg: Brachioradialis clearly active in curls; its share rises with the hand turned toward neutral/pronated (S on hand position).
muscles.role: Helps bend the elbow; library secondary.
muscles.surface: Thumb side of the upper forearm.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arm sags below shoulder height.

sources.citation: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MA, Vieira TM. 2009. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29.
sources.what_it_gave: Standing, incline (shoulder extended) and preacher curls: biceps long head at least 50 % of max RMS in all; shoulder position shifts where in the range the biceps works hardest.

sources.citation: Larsen S, Sandvik Kristiansen B, Osteras Sandberg N, et al. 2026. The effects of shoulder extension angle on elbow flexor hypertrophy in the cable curl exercise. Front Physiol 17:1750722.
sources.what_it_gave: Unilateral cable curls from a low pulley with the upper arm by the side (neutral) vs held back in shoulder extension: elbow flexors grew ~7-9 % in both; the shoulder angle made no clear difference.

clip_check.check: Upper arm level at shoulder height
Start nearly straight, end hand by the head
Fist closed on the handle; cable to the high pulley
Biceps strongest red, working arm only
